title: Adic formal smoothness ascends and descends through a smooth complete local map
statement: Let $R\to C\to H$ be local homomorphisms of commutative Noetherian local rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]; local means having a unique maximal ideal and sending the source maximal ideal into the target maximal ideal. Assume that $C$ and $H$ are complete for their maximal-ideal-adic topologies [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and that $C\to H$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_H$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. No completeness assumption on $R$ and no separability assumption on residue field extensions is imposed. Then $R\to C$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology if and only if $R\to H$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_H$-adic topology.

source.place: Tag 07PM, proposition-fs-regular, (1) iff (4), Tag 07NT, lemma-regular-permanence, and Tag 07ED, lemma-formally-smooth-completion. This is the algebraic argument in stacks-geometry.tex Tag 0DZS, lemma-characterize-smoothness, second paragraph; ascending direction is lemma-compose-formally-smooth.

proof.text: For ascent write $i:C\to H$. In a square-zero lifting problem $\alpha:R\to D$, $J^2=0$, $g:H\to D/J$ with $g(\mathfrak m_H^n)=0$, locality gives $gi(\mathfrak m_C^n)=0$. Formal smoothness of $C/R$ gives a lift $a:C\to D$ of $gi$, with $a|_R=\alpha$. Make $D$ a $C$-algebra by $a$; then $g$ is a $C$-algebra map. Formal smoothness of $H/C$ gives a $C$-algebra lift $b:H\to D$. Thus $b|_R=\alpha$ and $qb=g$, proving ascent directly from the lifting definition. No new composition lemma is needed.

source.place: lemma-compose-formally-smooth, its diagram hint, expanded for local adic maps; Definition 07NI and Lemma 07EC.

proof.text: For descent assume $R\to H$ is adically formally smooth. Put $A=\widehat R$, with canonical map $c:R\to A$. The completion is Noetherian by lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian, local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m_RA$ by lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring, and complete for that ideal by lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-ideal. The local maps $R\to C,H$ induce compatible maps on quotients by each maximal-ideal power, hence maps from $A$ to $\widehat C,\widehat H$. Identify these last two completions with $C,H$ by their assumed completeness. This defines local maps $f:A\to C$ and $h:A\to H$: the generators from $\mathfrak m_R$ map into the respective maximal ideals. If $i:C\to H$ is the given map, then $if=h$, since their coordinates modulo every $\mathfrak m_H^n$ agree, and completeness includes injectivity into the inverse limit. By lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-complete-source-target applied to $R\to H$, $h$ is formally smooth for the $\mathfrak m_H$-adic topology. The identification $\widehat H=H$ takes the extended maximal ideal to $\mathfrak m_H$.

source.place: Tags 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion), 07PM (proposition-fs-regular), 07NT (lemma-regular-permanence); the descent argument of stacks-geometry.tex Tag 0DZS (lemma-characterize-smoothness), second paragraph.

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-complete-local-regular to $h:A\to H$; both rings are now complete Noetherian local rings, so $h$ is regular. The given adic formal smoothness of $i:C\to H$ implies flatness by lem-weil-pbc-fs-adic-local-flat. Since $i$ is local, lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat supplies surjectivity of $\operatorname{Spec}H\to\operatorname{Spec}C$. Thus lem-weil-pbc-regular-permanence applies to $A\to C\to H$ and proves that $f:A\to C$ is regular.

source.place: Tags 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion), 07PM (proposition-fs-regular), 07NT (lemma-regular-permanence); the descent argument of stacks-geometry.tex Tag 0DZS (lemma-characterize-smoothness), second paragraph.

proof.text: Let $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$ and $B=C/\mathfrak m_AC$. By the definition of a regular ring map, $f$ is flat and its closed fibre $B=C\otimes_Ak$ is Noetherian and geometrically regular over $k$. It is local with maximal ideal the image of $\mathfrak m_C$, since it is a quotient of the local ring $C$ by the proper ideal $\mathfrak m_AC\subseteq\mathfrak m_C$. Apply lem-sfb-geometrically-regular-local-field-adic-smooth to this $k$-algebra $B$. Its conclusion is exactly adic formal smoothness of the closed fibre required by lem-weil-pbc-flat-formally-smooth-closed-fibre-adic, which therefore proves adic formal smoothness of $f:A\to C$. In particular no separability condition on $k\to C/\mathfrak m_C$ is inserted.

source.place: Tags 07ED (lemma-formally-smooth-completion), 07PM (proposition-fs-regular), 07NT (lemma-regular-permanence); the descent argument of stacks-geometry.tex Tag 0DZS (lemma-characterize-smoothness), second paragraph.

proof.text: Return to an arbitrary lifting problem for $R\to C$: let $\alpha:R\to D$, $J^2=0$, and $g:C\to D/J$ with $g(\mathfrak m_C^n)=0$ and $q\alpha=gfc$. Locality gives $\alpha(\mathfrak m_R^n)\subseteq J$, hence $\alpha(\mathfrak m_R^{2n})=0$. Factor $\alpha$ through $R/\mathfrak m_R^{2n}$ and compose with the coordinate projection of $A$ to define $\widehat\alpha:A\to D$. By lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-mod-power this extends $\alpha$ and kills $\mathfrak m_R^{2n}A=\mathfrak m_A^{2n}$. Also $gf$ kills $\mathfrak m_A^n$, since $f$ is local. Consequently $q\widehat\alpha$ and $gf$ both factor through $A/\mathfrak m_A^{2n}\cong R/\mathfrak m_R^{2n}$ and agree there: every class has a representative in $R$, where the original square commutes. Give $D$ its $A$-algebra structure via $\widehat\alpha$. The adic formal smoothness of $f$ from the preceding step gives an $A$-algebra lift $b:C\to D$ of $g$. Its restriction to $R$ is $\widehat\alpha c=\alpha$. This solves every original lifting problem and proves descent.
